Munajat-e-Maqbool

Tuesday

Fourth manzil · supplications 117 to 150

Opening praise

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

We praise You, O best of those in whom hope is placed and most generous of those from whom anything is sought, for teaching us Munajat-e-Maqbool, which brings nearness to Allah, and the supplications of the Messenger. Send perfect blessings upon him for as long as the west and east winds blow, and branches spring from their roots. Then we ask You for what we are about to recite. Ours is to ask, and Yours is to grant acceptance.

How to read

Read this opening invocation before each daily portion. Begin on Saturday, read one portion each day in order, and complete the cycle on Friday.

Swipe right to left to turn the page

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

Supplication117

Life and worship for Allah

O Allah, my prayer, my worship, my life and my death are for You. To You is my return, and to You, my Lord, belongs all that I leave behind.

Original commentary 117

This supplication teaches the great lesson that our prayers, our sacrifices, and indeed every part of our lives should be directed towards pleasing Allah. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) taught that, if this intention is set right, our eating, drinking, sleeping and waking can all become worship.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 80 · excerpt

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3520

Excerpt. Al-Tirmidhi: its chain is not strong; Darussalam: daif. Exact selected passage appears within the Arafah supplication.

Both 115 and 117 are excerpts of this same report; the shared source has a weak chain according to the cited assessments.

Supplication118

Goodness brought by the winds

O Allah, I ask You for the good of what the winds bring.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 80 · variant

Sahih Ibn Khuzayma 2841

Variant. Ibn Khuzayma explicitly suspends acceptance and does not regard its transmission as established. The request appears in the Arafah narration with singular al-rih; the compilation uses plural al-riyah. Bayhaqi Shuab 3842 gives the plural variant.

Ibn Khuzayma explicitly questions this particular report. Its presence in a work titled Sahih Ibn Khuzayma does not establish his authentication of it.

Supplication119

Gratitude, remembrance and surrendered hearts

O Allah, make me give You abundant thanks, remember You often, follow Your counsel and keep Your instructions. O Allah, our hearts, our forelocks and our limbs are in Your hand; You have not given us control over any of them. Since You have made us so, be our Guardian and guide us to the straight path.

Original commentary 119

This supplication asks: O Allah, make me a grateful servant who remembers You often, follows Your counsel and obeys Your instructions. O Allah, our hearts and all our limbs are in Your grasp. We ask You to be our Protector and show us the straight path.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 81 · composite

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3604m 2

Component: Opening four requests through preserving Your instruction. Al-Mubarakfuri: al-Faraj ibn Fadala in its chain is weak (Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi 9/120). Exact first sentence; numbering is 3604, supplement 2, in the cited Bashshar edition.

Al-Khatib, Tarikh Baghdad 13/199

Component: Hearts and forelocks in Your hand; guardianship and guidance. Al-Albani: very weak, al-Silsila al-Daifa 2909. The hearts/forelocks wording and guidance ending occur here. The compilation also incorporates the limbs variant found in Hilyat al-Awliya and adapts pronouns.

Abu Nuaym, Hilyat al-Awliya 8/367–368

Component: Our hearts and limbs are in Your hand; guardianship over them. Al-Albani: very weak for the hearts/ limbs report, Daif al-Jami 1185. Maruf al-Karkhi recites the hearts-and-limbs wording; the chain given here stops with Sufyan al-Thawri. The complete hearts-and-forelocks route appears in Tarikh Baghdad.

Al-Albani, Daif al-Jami 1185

Component: Critical grading of the hearts/limbs variant. Al-Albani: very weak. This grading concerns the hearts-and-limbs wording. Tarikh Baghdad records the corresponding hearts-and-forelocks variant.

Composite of separately transmitted prayers, including hearts/forelocks and hearts/limbs variants, with adapted pronouns. The components are traceable, but no single authenticated report for the full paragraph was verified.

Supplication120

Love of Allah and longing to meet Him

O Allah, make love for You the dearest of all things to me, and make fear of You greater to me than every other fear. Free me from worldly needs through longing to meet You. And when You bring comfort to the eyes of worldly people through their worldly life, bring comfort to my eyes through worshipping You.

Original commentary 120

This supplication asks that love for Allah become dearer than everything in creation, and that fear of Allah become greater than every other fear. It asks for a longing to meet Allah, and concludes by asking Him to make His worship a source of comfort to one's eyes.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 82 · variant

Abu Nuaym, Hilyat al-Awliya 8/282

Variant. Al-Albani: daif, Daif al-Jami 1164. Same complete prayer; primary Hilya wording has khawfak/ilayya, while the compilation has khashyatka/indi.

This route passes from al-Haytham ibn Malik to the Prophet without a Companion in the chain; the cited grading is weak.

Supplication121

Health, chastity and trustworthiness

O Allah, I ask You for good health, chastity, trustworthiness, good character and contentment with Your decree.

This is a short and remarkable supplication, asking for health, trustworthiness, good character and contentment with the divine decree.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 83 · exact

Al-Bukhari, al-Adab al-Mufrad 307

Exact. Al-Haythami identifies Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn Anum as weak, while noting some considered him trustworthy (Majma al-Zawaid 10/176). Full five requests match the primary text.

Supplication124

Reverence and happiness through obedience

O Allah, make me fear You as though I see You, always, until I meet You. Make me fortunate through mindfulness of You, and do not make me wretched through disobedience to You.

Original commentary 124

This supplication makes a remarkable request: O Allah, place awareness and fear of You in my heart as though I see You at every moment, and grant me the good fortune of piety. It ends by asking: O Allah, do not make me wretched and unfortunate through disobedience to You.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 84 · variant

Al-Tabarani, al-Mujam al-Awsat 5982

Variant. Al-Albani: very weak in its full form, al-Silsila al-Daifa 7047. Opening of a longer supplication; source has hatta ka-anni arak where compilation omits the first hatta.

The full report is graded very weak by al-Albani. Familiar individual expressions found elsewhere do not authenticate this longer wording.

Supplication125

Ease, well-being and pardon

O Allah, be gracious to me by making every difficulty easy, for making every difficulty easy is easy for You. I ask You for ease and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, pardon me, for You are Most Pardoning, Most Generous.

Original commentary 125

In this supplication, a person pleads his helplessness, weakness and difficulties, and asks for ease in this world and the Hereafter. At the end, we are taught to seek forgiveness by invoking Allah's generosity. Akbar Allahabadi expressed this meaning beautifully: 'Is He not able to gladden this one heart of mine—He who brought both worlds into being with a single “Be”?'

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 85 · composite

Al-Tabarani, al-Mujam al-Awsat 1250

Component: Ease in difficulties and well-being in both worlds. Al-Sanani: unknown narrators in its chain; al-Bayhaqi notes weakness in Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim. Exact substance; li in al-Tabarani and bi in al-Dulabi 2067 are preserved variants.

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3513

Parallel only: Closing request for pardon and the divine names Afuww and Karim. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan sahih; Darussalam: sahih. Related Laylat al-Qadr prayer has a different order and includes tuhibb al-afw; not an exact source for the book’s final sentence.

The concluding sentence is an adaptation of the well-known pardon prayer. Its authenticity does not authenticate the preceding ease report.

Recite this supplication repeatedly. It asks for purification and cleansing from hypocrisy of the heart, showing off, lying, treachery of the eyes and sins hidden in the heart.

O Allah, grant me well-being through Your power and admit me into Your mercy. Let my allotted life pass in obedience to You, make my final deed my best deed, and make Paradise its reward.

This supplication teaches us to ask for the removal of worry, sorrow and restlessness. It ends by invoking Allah's attributes of compassion and mercy: O Allah, I seek such mercy from You that it makes me independent of everyone besides You.

By invoking Allah as the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, this supplication asks: O Allah, accept our prayer, grant us our aims and make us independent of Your creation.

Al-Haythami, Kashf al-Astar 3103

Variant: all except added asaluka. Al-Haythami: Dawud ibn Abd al-Hamid is weak, Majma al-Zawaid 10/118. Bazzar narration preserved in Kashf al-Astar contains the full middle passage including ilayka yaud al-salam; asaluka appears in Bayhaqi’s parallel 46.

Supplication134

The life of the Hereafter

O Allah, there is no true life of bliss except the life of the Hereafter.

Original commentary 134

This supplication states a remarkable truth. May Allah make its meaning settle in our hearts: true bliss belongs to the Hereafter. Can worldly pleasure really be called bliss? Even if someone were given all the wealth in the world, how many days would that pleasure last? Hazrat Majzub (may Allah have mercy on him) put it beautifully: 'How few are the days of worldly pleasure! Do not lose Paradise's delights for their sake. If you do this, O heart, understand what you have done: foolish one, you have traded flowers for straw.'

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 90 · excerpt

Sahih al-Bukhari 6413

Excerpt. Included in Sahih al-Bukhari. Exact opening clause; report continues with prayer for Ansar and Muhajirun.

Supplication137

Mercy that puts life in order

O Allah, I ask You for a mercy from You by which You guide my heart, bring order to my affairs, mend my scattered state, set right my religion, settle my debts, protect what is absent from me, raise what is present with me, brighten my face, purify my deeds, inspire me with right guidance and restore harmony in my life, and through it protect me from every evil.

Original commentary 137

This is a long supplication asking for a special mercy from Allah. It explains this by asking: Grant me such mercy that my heart finds coolness and comfort, and such mercy that my worries are removed. At the end, it asks for such mercy as will protect me from every evil.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 91 · composite

This version includes the requests concerning religion, what is absent, and a brightened face. The order differs, and it does not contain the debt clause. Its inclusion in a collection titled Sahih does not override the cited critical assessment.

Abu Talib al-Makki Qut al-Qulub 1/12

Component: Settle my debt (wa-taqdi biha dayni). Not assessed; devotional book attestation, not independent hadith authentication. This early devotional work includes the exact debt clause in its version of the longer Ibn Abbas prayer.

Main wording combines variants of the long Ibn Abbas report in Tirmidhi 3419 and Ibn Khuzayma 1119, both critically graded weak. The extra debt clause is attested in al-Makkis Qut al-Qulub 1/12, but no independently authenticated hadith route was verified for it. Clause order and some wording differ.

Supplication141

O Allah, I lay my need before You. Though my understanding is limited and my deeds are weak, I am in need of Your mercy. Supplication144

Reliance after supplication

O Allah, this is our supplication, and Yours is to answer. This is our effort, and upon You is our reliance. O Allah, do not leave me to my own self even for the blink of an eye, and do not take away from me the good You have granted me.

Original commentary 144

This prayer should be recited at the end of every supplication. Its meaning is: O Allah, this helpless servant has presented his request; Yours is to accept it, and upon You alone is our reliance. O Allah, do not leave this helpless servant to his own self even for the blink of an eye. Do not take back from me the blessings You have granted me.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 96 · composite

Jami at-Tirmidhi 3419

Variant: Opening two sentences about supplication, effort and reliance. Da'if (Darussalam), as displayed by Sunnah.com.

Al-Daraqutni, al-Ilal 2816

Component: Do not leave me to myself; do not remove the good You have given. Al-Daraqutni: the correct route is mursal from Ubayd ibn Umayr. Both remaining clauses occur in the cited prayer; compilation adds an invocation and adapts wording.

The opening comes from the weak Tirmidhi 3419 report. Al-Daraqutni traces the remaining pair of requests to a mursal route, so the full sequence is not one authenticated narration. The recommendation to recite this after every supplication belongs to the original commentary and is not established as a general Prophetic instruction by these sources.

Supplication145

The eternal Lord without partner

O Allah, You are not a god we have brought into being, nor a lord we have invented whose remembrance fades away. You have no partners who share in Your judgement. Before You, we had no god to whom we could turn for refuge and abandon You. Nor has anyone helped You to create us, that we should associate him with You. Blessed and exalted are You. We ask You—there is no god but You—to forgive me.

Original commentary 145

This prayer asks: O Allah, we have no other god, and You have no partner. Our final refuge is Your Being alone. We ask You alone to pardon and forgive us.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 97 · composite

Al-Tabarani, al-Dua 1450

Component: Main praise through tabarakta wa-taalayta. Al-Haythami: Amr ibn al-Husayn al-Uqayli is abandoned, Majma al-Zawaid 10/186; al-Hakim 5708 had called the chain sahih. Main clauses match; the extra phrase no partners judge with You and final ask/forgive me sentence are absent.

Abu al-Shaykh, al-Azama 114

Component: The nor a Lord whose remembrance fades variant. Not separately assessed; do not transfer al-Hakim’s grading to this separate route. Abu al-Shaykh’s version includes the clause about a Lord whose remembrance fades, but differs in its remaining wording.

Al-Bayhaqi al-Daawat al-Kabir 70

Component: Lord whose remembrance fades; partners judging; concluding la ilaha illa anta ighfir li. Not assessed; no grading verified for this Aisha route. Bayhaqi’s text, vol. 1 p. 136, includes the partners clause and the closing request for forgiveness. It opens inna nushhiduka rather than the compilation’s opening, and does not contain its separate connecting word nas’aluka.

Supplication146

Entrusting the soul at bedtime

O Allah, You created my soul, and You will take it in death. Its death and its life belong to You. If You keep it alive, protect it with the protection You give Your righteous servants. If You cause it to die, forgive it and have mercy on it.

Original commentary 146

This prayer asks Allah: You are our Creator, and our life and death are in Your hands. We ask You to protect us during our lives as You protect Your righteous servants. If You cause us to die, O Allah, treat us with forgiveness and mercy.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 98 · composite

Sahih Muslim 2712

Component: Created my soul; death and life; preserve it if alive, forgive it if dead. Included in Sahih Muslim. Main supplication matches, except inserted anta and added protection qualifier/mercy request.

Sahih al-Bukhari 6320

Component: Preserve it as You preserve Your righteous servants; have mercy on it if held. Included in Sahih al-Bukhari. Protection qualifier and mercy request come from this related but differently structured bedtime supplication.

A combination of two authentic bedtime reports, not the verbatim wording of either report alone.

Supplication147

Knowledge, forbearance and well-being

O Allah, help me through knowledge, adorn me with forbearance, honour me with piety, and beautify me with well-being.

Original commentary 147

This prayer beautifully asks for knowledge, dignity, piety, and peace, thereby teaching us to ask for the blessings of both worlds.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 98 · variant

Al-Rafii, al-Tadwin fi Akhbar Qazwin 2/324

Variant: all except first verb. Al-Albani: daif, al-Silsila al-Daifa 3278. Primary text reads aghnini bil-ilm (enrich me through knowledge); the supplied text reads ainni bil-ilm (help me through knowledge).

The original edition, printed p. 80, has ainni, meaning help me, and its Urdu translation agrees. The located report has aghnini, meaning enrich me. The original wording has been retained as a source variant.

Supplication148

A time that honours knowledge and forbearance

O Allah, may I not live to see a time, nor may these people reach a time, when the learned are not followed and the forbearing are not treated with respect. Their hearts are those of non-Arabs, while their tongues are those of Arabs.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 99 · variant

Musnad Ahmad 22930

Variant: all except altered pronoun in second clause. Al-Albani: daif, Daif al-Targhib 82. Qurtuba edition: 5/340, no. 22930; Risala edition: no. 22879. The report has nor may you encounter, while the original compilation has nor may they encounter.

The original edition, printed p. 81, has the third-person wording nor may they encounter, supported by its Urdu translation. The located Ahmad report addresses the listeners in the second person. The source variant is retained. The report’s contrast concerns outward Arabic speech alongside failure to honour knowledge and restraint; it does not justify a general ethnic judgement.

Supplication149

Mercy for anyone harmed

O Allah, I take from You a pledge that You will never break with me. I am only human: whichever believer I have hurt, insulted, or struck, or cursed, make it a blessing, a purification, and a means of nearness by which You bring him close to You.

Original commentary 149

In this prayer, the sinless Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taught his community a profound lesson. Its meaning is: O Allah, I am human. If I hurt anyone, speak harshly to him, or pray against him, turn that prayer into mercy for him. How compassionate Allah is, teaching a prayer in which even a prayer against someone is made into a prayer for mercy.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 99 · variant

Sahih Muslim 2601b

Variant. Included in Sahih Muslim. Full covenant prayer matches closely; order and conjunctions of harm vary and the final Day of Resurrection phrase is omitted.

In Sahih Muslim these are the Prophet’s own words concerning his covenant with Allah. The narration does not establish a general promise that anyone’s hurtful speech or conduct becomes a blessing merely by reciting this prayer.

Supplication150

Comprehensive refuge from harm and the Fire

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from leucoderma, discord, hypocrisy, bad character, and the evil of all that You know. I seek refuge in Allah from the condition of the people of the Fire, from the Fire itself, and from any word or deed that brings one close to it; and from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold.

I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil that comes after it; from the evil of my own self, the evil of Satan and his enticement to associate partners with You; from our bringing evil upon ourselves or upon another Muslim; from my committing an error or sin that You do not forgive; and from the distress of standing on the Day of Resurrection.

Original commentary 150

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hypocrisy, bad character, and the evil of everything You know. Reform my deeds and character so that I may be saved from the punishment of Hell that they could bring upon me. This prayer teaches us to seek protection from the evils of today and the day that follows it. Along with this, it makes the request: O Allah, protect me from a sin on account of which I might remain unforgiven, and save me from the hardships and suffering of the Day of Resurrection. Its plea is: O Allah, You are to fill Paradise too, so grant us entry into Paradise without reckoning. Hazrat Majzub, may Allah have mercy on him, expressed it beautifully:
You will admit millions upon millions to Paradise;
Let this unworthy one be among them too.

Sources and notesTuesday · Prayer p. 100 · composite

Sunan Abi Dawud 1554

Component: Opening refuge from baras. Sahih (al-Albani). The compilation excerpts baras from a four-item prayer about illnesses.

Sunan Abi Dawud 1546

Component: Discord, hypocrisy and bad character. Daif (al-Albani). Exact three categories.

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3407

Component: The evil of what You know. Hasan (Darussalam). Exact clause within a longer prayer taught by Shaddad ibn Aws.

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3599

Component: I seek refuge in Allah from the condition of the people of the Fire. Daif (Darussalam); al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib. The final clause matches. Al-Albani’s authentication of the earlier beneficial-knowledge clauses excludes the ending beginning al-hamdu lillah (Daif al-Tirmidhi 3599); it does not authenticate this closing request.

Sunan Ibn Majah 3846

Component: The Fire and words or deeds bringing one near it. Sahih (Darussalam). This clause comes from Aisha’s comprehensive supplication.

Sahih Muslim 2713a

Component: Evil of everything whose forelock You hold. Reported in Sahih Muslim. The report says min sharri kulli shayin anta akhidhun binasiyatihi; the compilation says min sharri ma anta akhidhun binasiyatihi.

Sahih Muslim 2723b

Component: Evil of this day and what follows. Reported in Sahih Muslim. The report gives the evening wording and states that the Prophet said the corresponding wording in the morning; this is the morning adaptation.

Sunan Abi Dawud 5067

Component: My own evil, Satan and his shirk. Sahih (al-Albani). The Arabic here vocalizes shirkihi as in the compilation; another narration vocalizes sharakihi (his snare).

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3529

Component: Doing evil to ourselves or bringing it upon a Muslim. Hasan (Darussalam); al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib. Singular aqtarifa ala nafsi / ajurrahu is adapted to plural naqtarifa ala anfusina / najurrahu.

Musnad Ahmad 21666

Component: Committing an error or an unforgiven sin. Shuayb al-Arnaut: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam in its chain is weak. The longer report includes the qualifier muhbitatan, meaning nullifying deeds, which this compilation omits. It also has a sin that is not forgiven, where the compilation says a sin that You do not forgive. This report supplies only this component, not the complete entry.

Sunan an-Nasai 1617

Component: Constricted standing on the Day of Resurrection. Hasan (Darussalam). Exact final phrase in an opening prayer for night worship.

This compilation joins reports of differing grades, with shortened wording and changes of pronoun. No single report was established for the entire sequence. The English follows the original vocalisation shirkihi; the alternative sharakihi means his snare. The original commentary’s appeal for entry into Paradise without reckoning is a devotional reflection, not part of the Arabic or a promised reward for reciting this compilation.

ClosingDurood

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them peace in abundance.

Note from the Urdu edition

Recite Durood at the beginning and end of every manzil. This is a means for supplications to be accepted. (See page 64 of the original edition.)

Couplet from the closing page

If you are faithful to Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), We are yours;
what is this world? The Tablet and the Pen are yours.

Reference review

The source’s instruction is retained above. Praise and blessings before duʿā have support in Abu Dawud 1481; the weekly arrangement is the compiler’s. The specific eighty-year reward quoted with Monday’s Durood has not been established as sound. See general references G1 and G3.

General blessings upon the Prophet are supported by Qur’an 33:56. A general encouragement does not by itself establish a particular count, occasion or reward.
